get.description:
Report that the process is up and answering requests.

Liveness only: nothing beyond the process itself is consulted, so
an instance whose dependencies are gone still answers 200 here and
relies on the readiness probe to be taken out of rotation.

Refuse traffic unless every dependency this instance needs answers.

A readiness probe that reports the process rather than its
dependencies sends traffic to an instance whose first authenticated
request will fail, so the failure is a 503 - the status an
orchestrator is configured to act on - and never a 4xx. The raw
store's root is always probed; the database is probed only when
this instance was wired with a pool.

post.description:
Verify username and password, then start a session.

Needs no credential. A successful login sets the session cookie and
returns the subject, its display name and the session's CSRF token,
which cookie-authenticated state-changing requests must echo in the
``X-Huron-CSRF`` header. Answers 401 when password login is disabled
for this deployment, and 401 with one identical message - after the
same amount of work - whether the username is unknown, the account is
disabled, the name belongs to a service account, or the password is
wrong, so the response reveals nothing about which it was.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

401.description: password login is disabled, or the credential is wrong

post.description:
Revoke the session behind this request, if any, and clear the cookie.

Requires a credential (401 without one) but no particular role. A
cookie-authenticated caller must send the ``X-Huron-CSRF`` header, as
on every state-changing request; its session is revoked and takes
effect on the next request. A bearer caller has no session to revoke
and is simply acknowledged. The cookie is cleared either way.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

get.description:
Begin a browser login with the configured identity provider.

Needs no credential. Answers 302 to the provider's authorization
endpoint, with PKCE, and sets the transient ``huron_login`` cookie that
the callback needs to finish the flow; the cookie lives ten minutes and
never leaves ``/auth``. ``return_to`` is the local path the browser lands
on once login completes; a value that is not a local path is replaced
by ``/`` rather than refused. Answers 404 when this deployment has no
identity provider.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

get.description:
Finish a browser login: exchange the provider's code for a session.

The identity provider sends the browser here with ``code`` and
``state``. The pending login is read from the ``huron_login`` cookie
that ``/auth/oidc/start`` set; ``state`` must match it, and the code is
exchanged and the resulting ID token verified against the provider. A
first login provisions the user, a later one refreshes the display
name. A local account is never auto-linked to an identity provider: if
this is a first-ever login for the provider's subject and that subject
is already a local account's username, the login is refused rather
than the two identities merged. A disabled principal never gets a
session, no matter how it was provisioned - the same refusal a
disabled password login answers. On success the session cookie is set,
the login cookie is cleared and the browser is sent, 302, to the web
application at the path the flow was started with. Answers 401 when
the login cookie is missing, expired or forged, when ``state`` does
not match, when the provider's response cannot be trusted, or when the
principal is disabled; 404 when this deployment has no identity
provider; 409 when the provider's subject collides with an existing
local account's username.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

401.description: the login flow or the provider's response could not be trusted, or the principal is disabled

409.description: the subject is already held by a local account

get.description:
Describe the caller: who they are, how they authenticated, what they may do.

Requires a credential (401 without one) but no particular role - every
principal may ask about itself. ``effective_roles`` lists, per scope,
the capabilities the caller's role bindings grant there, resolved from
the same bindings every guarded route consults, so it cannot disagree
with what the API will actually allow. ``csrf_token`` and
``expires_at`` are set only for a cookie session; a bearer credential
has no server-side session and reports ``null`` for both.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

get.description:
List the login methods this deployment accepts.

Needs no credential: the login page asks this before anyone is signed
in. ``password`` says whether ``POST /auth/login`` is enabled; ``oidc``
whether an identity provider is configured, in which case
``oidc_start_url`` is the path that begins a browser login and is
``null`` otherwise. It reveals nothing beyond what the login page must
render.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

post.description:
Create an organization.

Requires ``organization.create`` at SYSTEM scope. The slug must be unique
across the platform and can never change afterwards; a duplicate is
refused with 409. Replaying the same ``Idempotency-Key`` with the same
request returns the original organization instead of a 409; reusing the
key for a different request is refused with 409.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: organization slug already exists

get.description:
List every organization the caller may discover.

Organizations are ordered by slug. ``after`` continues from the cursor a
previous page returned; a cursor that is not a valid continuation is
refused with 400.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: cursor is not a valid continuation

get.description:
Fetch one organization by id.

An id that is absent or not discoverable by the caller is 404.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

patch.description:
Update an organization's title or description.

Requires ``organization.update`` on the organization. ``If-Match`` must
carry the organization's current ``version``; a stale value is refused
with 412 and nothing changes, and a header that does not name a version
at all is refused with 422. Slugs are immutable: a ``slug`` that differs
from the current one is refused with 409. Every successful update
advances ``version`` by one. An id that is absent or not discoverable by
the caller is 404.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: the slug on an existing organization cannot change

412.description: If-Match does not match the current version

post.description:
Create a project in an organization.

Requires ``project.create`` on the organization. The slug must be unique
within the organization and can never change afterwards; a duplicate is
refused with 409. ``data_classification`` must be one of the platform's
configured classifications, or the request is refused with 400. An
organization id that is absent or not discoverable by the caller is
404. Replaying the same ``Idempotency-Key`` with the same request
returns the original project instead of a 409; reusing the key for a
different request is refused with 409.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: project slug already exists

get.description:
List the projects of an organization that the caller may discover.

Projects are ordered by slug. ``after`` continues from the cursor a
previous page returned; a cursor that is not a valid continuation is
refused with 400. An organization id that is absent or not discoverable
by the caller is 404, never an empty page.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: cursor is not a valid continuation

get.description:
Fetch one project by id.

An id that is absent or not discoverable by the caller is 404.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

patch.description:
Update a project's title or description.

Requires ``project.update`` on the project. ``If-Match`` must carry the
project's current ``version``; a stale value is refused with 412 and
nothing changes, and a header that does not name a version at all is
refused with 422. Slugs are immutable: a ``slug`` that differs from the
current one is refused with 409. Every successful update advances
``version`` by one. An id that is absent or not discoverable by the
caller is 404.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: the slug on an existing project cannot change

412.description: If-Match does not match the current version

post.description:
Create a dataset in a project.

Requires ``dataset.create`` on the project. The slug must be unique
within the project and can never change afterwards; a duplicate is
refused with 409. ``entry_layer`` names where the dataset's data first
arrives: ``raw`` by default, or ``bronze`` or ``silver`` for data the
lake does not originate. The dataset is active from creation. A project
id that is absent or not discoverable by the caller is 404. Replaying
the same ``Idempotency-Key`` with the same request returns the original
dataset instead of a 409; reusing the key for a different request is
refused with 409.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: dataset slug already exists

get.description:
List the datasets of a project that the caller may discover.

Datasets are ordered by slug. ``after`` continues from the cursor a
previous page returned; a cursor that is not a valid continuation is
refused with 400. A project id that is absent or not discoverable by
the caller is 404, never an empty page.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: cursor is not a valid continuation

get.description:
Fetch one dataset by id.

An id that is absent or not discoverable by the caller is 404.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

patch.description:
Update a dataset's title or description.

Requires ``dataset.update`` on the dataset. ``If-Match`` must carry the
dataset's current ``version``; a stale value is refused with 412 and
nothing changes, and a header that does not name a version at all is
refused with 422. Slugs are immutable: a ``slug`` that differs from the
current one is refused with 409. Every successful update advances
``version`` by one. An id that is absent or not discoverable by the
caller is 404.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: the slug on an existing dataset cannot change

412.description: If-Match does not match the current version

post.description:
Tag a revision of a dataset as a release.

Requires ``release.create`` on the dataset. A tag resolves to exactly
one revision, forever: a tag the dataset already has is refused with
409, and the revision it names must already exist or the request is
404, as is a dataset id that is absent or not discoverable by the
caller. Replaying the same ``Idempotency-Key`` with the same request
returns the original release instead of a 409; reusing the key for a
different request is refused with 409.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: release tag already exists

get.description:
List the releases of a dataset the caller may discover.

Releases are ordered by tag. ``after`` continues from the cursor a
previous page returned; a cursor that is not a valid continuation is
refused with 400. A dataset id that is absent or not discoverable by
the caller is 404, never an empty page.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: cursor is not a valid continuation

get.description:
Resolve a release tag to the revision it names.

A tag resolves to the same revision forever. A tag the dataset does not
have is 404, and so is a tag on a dataset that is absent or not
discoverable by the caller.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

get.description:
List a dataset's layer workflow, annotated with what the caller may do in each layer.

Every layer is returned in promotion order (raw, bronze, silver, gold)
with what a promotion into it may read from, whether human principals
may write it, whether data may enter the lake there directly, whether it
is this dataset's entry layer, which deployable produces it, and - for
THIS caller - whether they may read and write it. A dataset id that is
absent or not discoverable by the caller is 404.

schema.title: Response List Layers Api V1 Datasets  Dataset Id  Layers Get

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

get.description:
Fetch one committed revision by id.

An id that names no revision, or one whose dataset the caller cannot
discover, is 404.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

404.description: no such revision, or its dataset is not visible

get.description:
Download the revision's stored manifest document.

Re-authorized against ``data.read@raw`` on every request; supports
``Range`` for a resumable download.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

404.description: no such revision, or its dataset is not visible

get.description:
Download one file of a revision's payload.

Only a path the stored manifest lists is served; re-authorized against
``data.read@raw`` on every request; supports ``Range`` for a resumable
download.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: the path breaks a storage-layout rule

404.description: no such revision, its dataset is not visible, or the manifest lists no such path

post.description:
Open a raw ingest session on an existing dataset.

Requires ``data.write`` on the dataset's raw layer; the dataset's
entry layer must be ``raw``. Plans every declared file for a complete independent upload and
locks the dataset until the
session reaches a terminal state. Replaying the same
``Idempotency-Key`` with the same files returns the original session
instead of a 409; reusing the key for a different manifest is refused.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: the manifest is empty or breaks a path rule

409.description: another session is already open, its entry layer is not raw, the manifest collides with an existing entry, the dataset already holds this manifest, or the idempotency key was reused for a different manifest

413.description: a file, or the revision as a whole, exceeds the configured limit

post.description:
Mint a raw dataset under a project, then open its first ingest session.

Requires ``data.write`` on the project's raw layer and
``dataset.create`` on the project; the minted dataset's entry layer is
always ``raw``. One ``Idempotency-Key`` covers both writes: the dataset
is created under a key derived from it, so a retry after a failure
between the two replays the kept dataset and opens the session on it,
while reusing the key for a different manifest is refused before a
second dataset is ever minted.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: the manifest is empty or breaks a path rule

409.description: another session is already open, the manifest collides with an existing entry, the dataset already holds this manifest, the idempotency key was reused for a different manifest, or the dataset slug already exists

413.description: a file, or the revision as a whole, exceeds the configured limit

get.description:
Fetch one ingest session and its ledger.

The owner, or a project admin, may read a session. An id that is
absent, or whose dataset is not discoverable, is 404; a visible
caller who is neither the owner nor a project admin is 403.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

post.description:
Renew a session's lease.

Only the owner may renew it, and only while their raw-write binding
still stands. The lease moves forward; ``etag`` does not.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: the session's lease has lapsed, or it is terminal

post.description:
Abort a session, releasing the dataset lock it holds.

The owner may abort their own session; a project admin may force-abort
anyone's. Never from COMMITTING: once a commit has begun it either
becomes durable or fails, never half of each.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: the session is already COMMITTING or terminal

412.description: the session moved under the caller

post.description:
Verify every submitted file and move the session to VERIFYING.

Every submitted file must already be COMPLETE; anything still pending
is refused with the incomplete paths named. The owner alone may drive
it, and only while their raw-write binding stands.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: not every planned file is complete

409.description: the session's lease has lapsed, or it is not UPLOADING

412.description: the session moved under the caller

post.description:
Publish a verified session's envelope as a committed revision.

Requires the current ``If-Match`` version, unless the session is
already COMMITTED, in which case the original revision is returned
unchanged. Replaying the same ``Idempotency-Key`` with the same
``manifest_sha256`` and metadata returns the original revision instead
of a second commit; reusing the key for a different request is
refused. The owner alone may drive it, and only while their raw-write
binding stands.

422.description: the If-Match header is malformed

500.description: storage and the catalog disagree about a committed revision

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: the declared manifest digest disagrees with the session's

409.description: the session's lease has lapsed, it is not VERIFYING or COMMITTING, the metadata submission violates the registered schema, the idempotency key was reused for a different request

412.description: the If-Match version disagrees with the session's current etag

put.description:
Stream one part's bytes into its range of the file's payload.

``Content-Length`` must equal the part's planned length; a request with
no ``Content-Length`` - a chunked body - is refused before a byte is
read, since the part's length must be known up front. The owner alone
may drive an upload, and only while their raw-write binding stands.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: the content length disagreed with the plan, the stream ended short or long, the file's observation disagreed with the manifest, or the client disconnected mid-body

404.description: no such file, or the part is outside its planned range

409.description: the session's lease has lapsed, it is not UPLOADING, or the file cannot receive a part in its current state

post.description:
Assemble and verify one file's uploaded parts.

Every part the plan calls for must already be recorded before this
succeeds; a mismatch against the manifest discards the assembled bytes
and resets the file to no parts recorded. The owner alone may drive it.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: the assembled bytes disagree with the manifest; every part must be re-sent

409.description: the session's lease has lapsed, it is not UPLOADING, or the file is not fully received or is already complete

get.description:
List every role in the catalog.

The role catalog: what each role can do and who may hold it. Each role
carries its control-plane capabilities, its layer-scoped data-plane
grants, the scopes it may be bound at and the kinds of principal that
may hold it. The catalog is fixed per deployment, so the whole of it is
returned at once and there is nothing to page.

schema.title: Response List Roles Api V1 Roles Get

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

get.description:
List the role bindings granted at SYSTEM scope.

Requires ``rbac.binding_manage`` at SYSTEM scope. Bindings are ordered
by principal, then role. ``after`` continues from the cursor a previous
page returned; a cursor that is not a valid continuation is refused
with 400.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: cursor is not a valid continuation

post.description:
Grant a role to a principal at SYSTEM scope.

Requires ``rbac.binding_manage`` at SYSTEM scope. A grant identical to
an existing one (same principal, role and scope) is refused with 409; a
role the catalog does not define, one this kind of principal may not
hold, or one that cannot be bound at SYSTEM scope is refused with 422.
With ``expires_in_days`` the grant lapses on its own; without it, the
grant stands until revoked.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: an identical role binding exists

delete.description:
Revoke a role binding granted at SYSTEM scope.

Requires ``rbac.binding_manage`` at SYSTEM scope. A binding that does
not exist, or that was granted at some other scope, is 404 either way:
this collection never confirms what was granted elsewhere. Success is
204 with no body.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

post.description:
Grant a role to a principal on an organization.

Requires ``rbac.binding_manage`` on the organization. An unknown

principal, role and scope) is refused with 409; a role the catalog does
not define, one this kind of principal may not hold, or one that cannot
be bound at organization scope is refused with 422. With
``expires_in_days`` the grant lapses on its own; without it, the grant
stands until revoked.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: an identical role binding exists

get.description:
List the role bindings granted on an organization.

Requires ``rbac.binding_manage`` on the organization. Only grants made

Bindings are ordered by principal, then role. ``after`` continues from
the cursor a previous page returned; a cursor that is not a valid
continuation is refused with 400. An unknown organization is 404.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: cursor is not a valid continuation

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: an identical role binding exists

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

post.description:

Requires ``rbac.binding_manage`` on the dataset. Only grants made at

organization or SYSTEM scope. Bindings are ordered by principal, then

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

delete.description:
Revoke a role binding granted on a dataset.

Requires ``rbac.binding_manage`` on the dataset. A binding that does
not exist, or that was granted at some other scope, is 404 either way:

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

post.description:
Create a service account in an organization.

Requires ``service_account.manage`` on the organization. ``name`` must
be slug-shaped and unique within the organization: a malformed name is
refused with 400 and a duplicate with 409. The account's subject - the
identity its keys authenticate as - is derived from the organization's
slug and the name. An unknown organization is 404.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: service account already exists

get.description:
List the service accounts of an organization.

Requires ``service_account.manage`` on the organization. Accounts are
ordered by name, disabled ones included. ``after`` continues from the
cursor a previous page returned; a cursor that is not a valid
continuation is refused with 400. An unknown organization is 404.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: cursor is not a valid continuation

post.description:
Issue an API key that authenticates as a service account.

Requires ``service_account.manage`` on the organization. The key
authenticates AS the service account: it carries the account's
intrinsic authority and nothing of the caller's own. An account that
has been disabled is refused with 403; an unknown account, or one
owned by a different organization, is 404. The response is the only
time the key's secret is shown; it is never stored and cannot be
recovered.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

post.description:
Disable a service account and revoke every key it holds.

Requires ``service_account.manage`` on the organization. Once disabled,
no key issued to the account authenticates and no new key can be issued
for it; the API offers no way to re-enable it. Disabling is idempotent:
calling it again on an already-disabled account reports the original
``disabled_at`` and does not revoke keys a second time. An unknown
account, or one owned by a different organization, is 404.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

post.description:
Create a policy definition.

Creating a policy grants nothing - attachment is the guarded act - so
no capability beyond a credential is needed here. ``spec`` is the
caller's own JSON, stored and returned verbatim and never interpreted
by the service; a spec over 1 MiB in canonical form is refused with 422.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

get.description:
List every policy definition.

Policies are ordered by name, then id, since names are not unique.
``after`` continues from the cursor a previous page returned; a cursor
that is not a valid continuation is refused with 400.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

400.description: cursor is not a valid continuation

Attach a policy to an organization.

Requires ``organization.policy_attach`` on the organization. An unknown
organization or policy is 404; a policy already attached to this
organization is refused with 409.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: policy is already attached at this scope

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

409.description: policy is already attached at this scope

post.description:
Issue an API key for the calling principal.

The key is issued to the CALLING principal and keys never escalate: it
inherits the caller's subject and kind, so everything the key can do is
exactly what the caller's role bindings already allow. An
``Idempotency-Key`` header is required. The response is the only time
the key's secret is shown; it is never stored and cannot be recovered,
so a caller that loses it issues another key.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

post.description:
Provision a password user.

Requires ``user.manage`` at SYSTEM scope. The username becomes the
user's subject and must not be held by any existing principal - a
password user, an OIDC identity or a service account, disabled or not -
or the request is refused with 409: a password is attached to a subject
exactly once, at creation, never silently handed to an existing
identity.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: username is already taken

put.description:
Replace a user's password.

Requires ``user.manage`` at SYSTEM scope. Every session and every API
key the user holds is revoked before the acknowledgement is returned -
a reset logs the user out everywhere, and a key is a login that would
otherwise outlive it. An unknown principal is 404; one that is a
service account rather than a user is refused with 409.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: principal is not a user

post.description:
Disable a user, revoke every session they hold, and revoke every API key they hold.

Requires ``user.manage`` at SYSTEM scope. A disabled user can no longer
log in by any method - password, OIDC or a self-issued API key - and
the API offers no way to re-enable them. An unknown principal is 404;
one that is a service account rather than a user is refused with 409.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

409.description: principal is not a user

get.description:
Search the catalog.

The search projection is not configured, so every request is refused
with 503 ``PROJECTION_UNAVAILABLE``.

422.description: the request did not satisfy the declared schema

403.description: the principal's role bindings do not allow this

503.description: the search projection is not configured

AttachPolicy.title: AttachPolicy
AttachPolicy.description:
The body of a ``policy-attachments`` POST: which policy to bind to this scope.

The scope - an organization, a project or a dataset - is named by the
route, so the body carries only the policy's id. Attaching is the
guarded act; the same policy attached twice at one scope is refused
with ``ATTACHMENT_EXISTS``.

CommitIngestSession.title: CommitIngestSession
CommitIngestSession.description: Body of ``…/commit``: the declared identity, restated, and the final descriptive metadata.

CreateApiKey.title: CreateApiKey
CreateApiKey.description:
The body that asks for a new API key: what to call it and how far it reaches.

A key never widens what its owner may do; ``scopes`` and ``project_id``
only narrow it, and default to read-only with no project restriction.
``expires_in_days`` bounds the key's life to between a day and four
hundred, ninety by default: no key is issued without an expiry.

CreateDataset.title: CreateDataset
CreateDataset.description:
The body of ``POST /projects/{project_id}/datasets``.

``slug`` is the dataset's permanent name within its project - unique
there, immutable afterwards, and checked against the catalog's slug
rules. A profile (``profile_name`` and ``profile_version``) is required
of every dataset; ``entry_layer`` declares where its data first
arrives. A dataset is ``ACTIVE`` from the moment it is created.

CreateIngestSession.title: CreateIngestSession
CreateIngestSession.description:
Body of ``POST /datasets/{dataset_id}/ingest-sessions``: the files the revision will hold.

Emptiness is refused by the domain as ``EMPTY_REVISION``, not by a
``min_length`` here, so the client sees the same code whether the list
is empty or merely invalid in some other way.

CreateIngestSessionInProject.title: CreateIngestSessionInProject
CreateIngestSessionInProject.description:
Body of ``POST /projects/{project_id}/ingest-sessions``: a dataset to create and its files.

The intake creates the dataset, always with ``raw`` as its entry
layer, and opens the first session on it in one request.

CreateOrganization.title: CreateOrganization
CreateOrganization.description:
The body of ``POST /organizations``.

``slug`` is the organization's permanent name: unique across the
platform, immutable afterwards, and checked against the catalog's slug
rules and its reserved root names. ``description`` may be left empty.

CreatePolicy.title: CreatePolicy
CreatePolicy.description:
The body of ``POST /policies``: a definition that grants nothing until attached.

``policy_type`` is a lowercase identifier the caller's tooling switches
on; ``spec`` is the caller's own JSON object, stored and returned
verbatim and never interpreted by the service. The one thing checked
about ``spec`` is its size: at most ``MAX_POLICY_SPEC_BYTES`` (1 MiB)
in canonical form.

CreateProject.title: CreateProject
CreateProject.description:
The body of ``POST /organizations/{organization_id}/projects``.

``slug`` is the project's permanent name within its organization -
unique there, immutable afterwards, and checked against the catalog's
slug rules. ``data_classification`` must be a code from the
deployment's configured classification vocabulary; any other value is
refused with ``CLASSIFICATION_UNKNOWN``.

CreateRelease.title: CreateRelease
CreateRelease.description:
The body of ``POST /datasets/{dataset_id}/releases``: pin a tag to a revision.

``tag`` must be new for the dataset and follow the catalog's tag rules;
``revision_number`` must name a revision the dataset already has. Once
created, the tag resolves to that revision forever; it is never
repointed.

CreateRoleBinding.title: CreateRoleBinding
CreateRoleBinding.description: Grant ``role`` to ``principal`` at the scope named by the route.

CreateServiceAccount.title: CreateServiceAccount
CreateServiceAccount.description:
The body of ``POST /organizations/{organization_id}/service-accounts``.

``name`` is the account's label within the owning organization, which
the route names; it must be unique there, and a second account with
the same name is refused with ``SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EXISTS``. The account's
authority is fixed by its kind, so there is nothing else to declare.

CreateUser.title: CreateUser
CreateUser.description:
The body of ``POST /users``: provision a human who signs in with a password.

``username`` becomes the principal's subject - lowercase, two to
sixty-three characters - and must be held by no principal at all,
password or OIDC, enabled or disabled; a taken name is refused with
``USERNAME_TAKEN`` rather than silently attaching a password to an
existing identity. ``password`` is set exactly once here; afterwards
only an administrator's ``SetPassword`` replaces it.

DatasetView.title: DatasetView
DatasetView.description:
One dataset as the API publishes it.

``version`` is the value ``If-Match`` carries back on a PATCH; the
raw-store generation behind it is not part of this contract.
``lifecycle_state`` is the dataset's ``DatasetLifecycle`` name and
``entry_layer`` the layer its data first arrives in.

FileState.title: FileState
FileState.description:
Whether a planned file's bytes are in the envelope and proven.

``PENDING`` means the ledger does not yet vouch for the file's bytes,
whether none, some or all of its parts have arrived, or an observation
was found not to match and discarded. ``COMPLETE`` means the bytes are
proven: every part arrived and the whole-file observation matched the
manifest. There is no
third state; a mismatch never becomes one, it returns the file to
``PENDING``.

IngestFileView.title: IngestFileView
IngestFileView.description: One planned file and its progress: the plan and the ledger.

IngestSessionView.title: IngestSessionView
IngestSessionView.description: A session and its ledger; ``etag`` is what ``If-Match`` carries back on commit.

IngestState.title: IngestState
IngestState.description:
The normal, recovery and terminal states of one ingest session.

The happy path is ``PREPARING -> UPLOADING -> VERIFYING -> COMMITTING ->
COMMITTED``. ``ABORTED`` is available only before COMMITTING; ``FAILED``
is available from every nonterminal state. COMMITTING can re-enter itself
so a retry can finish after publication, or enter the fenced nonterminal
state RECOVERING. RECOVERING retains the session's claims and permits
only COMMITTED or FAILED next; it cannot abort or resume client work.
COMMITTED, ABORTED and FAILED are terminal.

IssuedApiKey.title: IssuedApiKey
IssuedApiKey.description:
A key at the one moment its secret exists in cleartext.

``secret`` is returned by this response and by nothing else in the
service: it is never stored, never logged, and cannot be re-read. A
caller that loses it issues another key.

IssuedServiceAccountKey.title: IssuedServiceAccountKey
IssuedServiceAccountKey.description: A key that authenticates AS the service account it names.

Layer.title: Layer
Layer.description:
The four storage layers, valued as the lower-case codes paths and the API use.

This enum is the one place the codes are spelled out; the path layout
and the API both derive their layer names from it.

LayerCapabilities.title: LayerCapabilities
LayerCapabilities.description: What the calling principal may do in one layer of one dataset.

LayerGrantView.title: LayerGrantView
LayerGrantView.description:
A data-plane capability limited to a set of layers.

``layers`` is ``null`` when the grant reaches every layer, mirroring
``Binding.layers`` rather than expanding it - the two are different
statements and a client that flattens them loses the distinction.

LayerView.title: LayerView
LayerView.description: One layer of the workflow, annotated with what the caller may do there.

LoginResult.title: LoginResult
LoginResult.description:
What a successful password login hands the browser.

``csrf_token`` is the double-submit token for this session and is
returned exactly once, to the caller that just proved the password.

ManifestFile.title: ManifestFile
ManifestFile.description: One declared file: the manifest entry as the client states it.

MetadataSubmission.title: MetadataSubmission
MetadataSubmission.description:
The committer's half of ``metadata.json``: description, never identity or provenance.

Extra fields are refused rather than silently dropped, so a client
that mistypes a member name or tries to set a server-sourced one
(``committed_by``, ``committed_at``) is told at the schema boundary
instead of having the value vanish. Content rules beyond shape -
non-empty titles, unique tags and the rest - belong to the registered
metadata schema, not to this model, so there is exactly one authority
for them.

NewDataset.title: NewDataset
NewDataset.description:
The dataset an intake creates before opening its first session.

Its entry layer is ``raw`` by definition - an intake exists to open a
raw ingest session - so the body carries no ``entry_layer`` field.

OrganizationView.title: OrganizationView
OrganizationView.description:
One organization as the API publishes it.

``version`` is the value ``If-Match`` carries back on a PATCH; the
raw-store ``generation`` behind it is not part of this contract.

PasswordLogin.title: PasswordLogin
PasswordLogin.description:
The body of ``POST /auth/login``: a username and the password proving it.

Both must be non-empty; nothing else is checked here. Whether the pair
names an enabled user with that password is decided by the login
route, which answers every failure identically.

PasswordReset.title: PasswordReset
PasswordReset.description:
The acknowledgement of a password reset.

Every session the user held was revoked before this was returned, so
``status`` (always ``password-reset``) also means "signed out
everywhere".

PatchDataset.title: PatchDataset
PatchDataset.description:
The body of ``PATCH /datasets/{dataset_id}``: the fields a caller may change.

A field left out or sent as ``null`` keeps its value. ``slug`` is
accepted only so that an attempted change is refused explicitly, with
``SLUG_IMMUTABLE``, rather than silently ignored; sending the current
slug is harmless. The patch is applied only against the version the
``If-Match`` header names.

PatchOrganization.title: PatchOrganization
PatchOrganization.description:
The body of ``PATCH /organizations/{organization_id}``: the changeable fields.

A field left out or sent as ``null`` keeps its value; the patch is
applied only against the version the ``If-Match`` header names.

PatchProject.title: PatchProject
PatchProject.description:
The body of ``PATCH /projects/{project_id}``: the changeable fields.

A field left out or sent as ``null`` keeps its value; the patch is
applied only against the version the ``If-Match`` header names. The
classification is fixed at creation and is not part of this body.

PolicyAttachmentView.title: PolicyAttachmentView
PolicyAttachmentView.description:
One policy bound to one scope.

``scope_type`` is never ``SYSTEM``: policies attach at an organization,
a project or a dataset, so ``scope_id`` always names one of those.

PolicyView.title: PolicyView
PolicyView.description:
A policy definition. Creating one grants nothing; attaching it does.

``spec`` is the caller's own JSON, stored and returned verbatim: the
service does not interpret it, so it is not typed beyond "an object".

ProjectView.title: ProjectView
ProjectView.description:
One project as the API publishes it.

``version`` is the value ``If-Match`` carries back on a PATCH; the
raw-store generation behind it is not part of this contract.

ProviderInfo.title: ProviderInfo
ProviderInfo.description:
What the login page renders from: the credential methods this deployment accepts.

Served unauthenticated by design - the page has no principal yet when
it needs this. ``oidc_start_url`` is the path that begins a browser
login when an identity provider is configured, and ``null`` when
``oidc`` is false.

ReleaseView.title: ReleaseView
ReleaseView.description: One release tag, resolving to exactly one revision, forever.

RevisionView.title: RevisionView
RevisionView.description: A committed revision as the catalog records it; the storage location is not wire contract.

RoleBindingView.title: RoleBindingView
RoleBindingView.description:
One grant of one role to one principal at one scope.

``scope_id`` is ``null`` if and only if ``scope_type`` is ``SYSTEM``;
every other scope names the organization, project or dataset the grant
was made at. ``expires_at`` is ``null`` for a grant that does not lapse.

RoleView.title: RoleView
RoleView.description:
One role in the catalog: what it can do and who may hold it.

Every collection field is sorted, because the role model stores them as
frozensets and a frozenset's iteration order is not stable across
processes.

ScopeRoles.title: ScopeRoles
ScopeRoles.description:
The capabilities this caller holds at one scope.

Grouped from the same compiled ``Binding`` set ``rbac.decide`` evaluates
for every guarded route, so this reports exactly what the guard chain
would allow at this scope rather than a role name reconstructed after
the fact - a compiled binding carries capability codes, not the role it
was compiled from, and re-deriving one would risk drifting from what is
actually enforced.

ScopeType.title: ScopeType
ScopeType.description:
The levels a binding can attach at, from the whole platform down to one dataset.

``SYSTEM`` contains every organization, an ``ORGANIZATION`` its
projects, a ``PROJECT`` its datasets; a binding covers the scope it is
attached to and everything nested inside it (see
:meth:`Binding.covers`).

ServiceAccountView.title: ServiceAccountView
ServiceAccountView.description:
A roleless identity owned by one organization.

``subject`` is the identity its API keys authenticate as; ``name`` is
unique within the owning organization and is what the collection is
ordered by. ``disabled_at`` set means every key it holds has been
revoked.

SessionInfo.title: SessionInfo
SessionInfo.description:
The answer to "who am I, and how was I authenticated".

Served by the unversioned ``GET /auth/session`` rather than a
versioned resource route: identity introspection is a login concern,
not a v1 resource. ``effective_roles`` is resolved from the same
binding set the authorization guards consult, so what a caller is told
it may do and what it is actually allowed to do cannot drift apart.
``csrf_token``/``expires_at`` are only ever set for a cookie-authenticated
caller; a bearer credential carries no server-side session to report.

SetPassword.title: SetPassword
SetPassword.description:
The body of ``PUT /users/{principal_id}/password``: the replacement password.

There are no reset tokens and no self-service change by design: an
administrator sets the new password, and every session the user held
is revoked when it takes effect.

SignOut.title: SignOut
SignOut.description:
The acknowledgement ``POST /auth/logout`` returns.

``status`` is always ``signed-out``: by the time this is sent, the
session behind the request (if there was one) is revoked and the
session cookie is cleared.

UploadAction.title: UploadAction
UploadAction.description: The upload disposition for one file's complete bytes.

UserView.title: UserView
UserView.description:
One admin-provisioned human, as the API publishes them.

The identity provider's subject for this person is not part of this
contract; neither is ``kind``, which every route returning this model
has already constrained to a user.

Problem.description:
The body of every response at or above 400 (RFC 9457).

``type``, ``title``, ``status`` and ``detail`` are the standard problem
members; ``code`` is the stable identifier a client switches on, from
which ``type`` (``urn:huron:error:<code>``) and ``title`` are derived,
and ``context`` carries structured detail such as validation errors or
failed readiness checks when there is any. The class exists for the
OpenAPI document - every error response ``$ref``s it - rather than for
construction: handlers build the body directly.
Problem.title: Problem
